# Draft:Nice Looking Man

A nice looking man can be defined as a man who is nice looking.
John
Within the year 1735, an individual of uncertain origin, only referred to in certain fragmented historical accounts, simply by "John" is portrayed to have articulated a singular and enigmatic utterance, "The,". While the authenticity and context of this statement remain common subjects of considerable debate, the attribution persists within niche academic circles. Some interpret John's minimalistic expression as emblematic of his remarkable presence, often described as belonging to the exceptional title of being a "nice looking man" of his time.
John Historian
Accounts of John's life are at best, speculative. Surviving references provide a lack of verifiable biographical details, which leaves historians to purely reconstruct his existence purely through inference and imaginative conjecture. Among more widely accepted assumptions, endorsed humorously yet persistently through commentary by John Historian, a self proclaimed historian, suggest that all human beings engage in the fundamental biological process of gas exchange, inhaling oxygen and exhaling carbon dioxide. While this may lack empirical evidence, reasonable suspicion has accepted the argument as reasonable.
Dylan Kurvink
In a more contemporary context, Dylan Kurvink can be interpreted as a modern exemplar of the same "nice-looking" archetype. Also commonly known as "Karl Marx Fortnite" and sometimes referred to as "Michael Cat" (short for Michelangelo Roman Catholic Church) due to his bond with Michael Dog, (short for Michelangelo Dog Day Afternoon), his perceived prominence derives not from documented achievements, but from his commentary on the socioeconomic condition of the modern world. Within his large body of commentary, one particular statement remains significant: "I have good news, and I have bad news."
Though simple to the human eye, this remark has been interpreted as indicative of a broader awareness of duality within circumstances. The assertion that he possesses both forms of news implies a degree of communicative intent. In the whimsical analytical framework that equates such qualities, this has been cited as further evidence supporting Kurvink's classification as a "nice-looking man".
